This petition is filed by the petitioners who are the legal representatives of deceased Kadappa.
This petition is filed to quash the impugned order passed in MVC No.1163/2015 dated 29.09.2022 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Ballari vide Annexure-J.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioners are none other than wife and children of deceased Kadappa and the said deceased Kadappa NC: 2024:KHC-D:7881 had filed a claim petition in MVC No.1163/2015 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-V at Ballari for the injuries suffered by him in the road traffic accident.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-V at Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said claim petition came to be allowed during the lifetime of late Sri Kadappa when compensation was awarded.
The said judgment and award of the Tribunal came to be challenged by the owner of the offending vehicle before this Court in MFA No.100569/2018.
The said appeal preferred by the owner came to be allowed.
However, the compensation was not altered, but the insurer was directed to pay the compensation with interest at the rate of 6%.
Thereby, the award passed by the Tribunal with regard to the petitioners or the late Kadappa does not get altered in the Miscellaneous First Appeal.
4. This being the state of affairs, the injured Kadappa died on 18.08.2020 that is subsequent to the orders of the appeal before this Court in MFA No.100569/2018.

Pursuant to the dismissal, the modification in the first appeal before this Court, the compensation amount came to be deposited before the Tribunal to an extent of 3,91,465/- by the insurer, but in view of death of deceased Kadappa, the petitioners who are the only LRs made an application before the Tribunal by filing an NC: 2024:KHC-D:7881 application under Order XXII Rule 9 along with an application for delay to permit them to come on record and disburse the amount in their favour as the original claimant had died pursuant to the award and the appeal preferred by the owner of the offending vehicle.

When the application was taken up by the Tribunal, there was no objections filed by the respondent therein, i.e., the Insurance Company or the owner of the offending vehicle or any other person or rival claimants claiming to be the LRs of deceased Kadappa to stake a claim over the compensation amount deposited by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal dismissed the application solely on the basis of the affidavit filed by the petitioners, they cannot be held that they are the only legal heirs of deceased Kadappa and there is no materials placed before the Court from Competent Authority and accordingly their applications came to be rejected.
5.
The petitioners being aggrieved by rejection of their application are before this Court.

The petitioners who are the wife and children of deceased Kadappa, the petitioners have produced Annexures-B, C, C1, D, D1 and D2 being the death certificate of Kadappa, the genealogy tree, the Aadhar cards, NC: 2024:KHC-D:7881 the affidavit and the other cards of themselves to show that they are the legal heirs of deceased Kadappa.
The Tribunal has not appreciated these documents despite there being no objections or rival claim.
The amount of compensation which was liable to be paid to the deceased Kadappa has been deposited before the Tribunal by the Insurance Company.

6. In the normal circumstances, this Court would have relegated the matter for determination of whether the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Kadappa as contemplated under Order XXII Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the appeal proceedings.

However, this is a writ petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India challenging the dismissal order of the application preferred by the petitioners who claim to be the LRs of deceased Kadappa and to prove the same, they have produced the documents mentioned herein above.

The Tribunal has to accept the documents so produced ex-facie, which are Government issued records, namely genealogy tree,

sentences.text: Same has not been done by the Tribunal, and has rejected the application.

7. In view of production of the documents stated herein above, which clearly go to show that the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased Kadappa, the Trial Court ought to have accepted the same and allow the application for claiming the compensation awarded in favour of deceased Kadappa 8.

Under the circumstances being satisfied with the documents produced by the petitioners and there being no rival claim made against deceased Kadappa for the claim amount or objections raised by the respondent in the claim petition, the Tribunal ought to have allowed the application ordered for release of the amount in favour of the petitioners.
Having not done so, the order passed by the Tribunal requires to be set aside.

It is also necessary to note that the Motor Vehicles Act being a social welfare legislation and the main object of the enactment for the welfare and benefit of the persons who are injured or effected in the road traffic accident, it is generally decided in a summary manner without asking for elaborate proof with regard to the details of the legal heirs, unless it is NC: 2024:KHC-D:7881 seriously objected by any third party.

Hence I pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is allowed.
ii) The application filed by the petitioners under Order XXII, Rule 3 is allowed.
iii) The petitioners shall be treated as the legal heirs of deceased Kadappa.
iv) The compensations were deposited by the insurance company i.e., respondent No.2 before the claim petition along with interest, shall be disbursed in favour of the petitioners herein.
v) In case there is any rival claim made by anyone whatsoever claiming to be the legal heirs or dependents of deceased Kadappa, the petitioners herein shall indemnify the said claimants.
